solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Porcelain victory award presented before local match

indicators.note: something presented before another comes first in the line, so the order of the two parts is set

parts.note: a crown is the prize for a champion
a derby is a game between two neighbouring teams

explanation.surface: A china trophy is handed out ahead of a game between neighbouring rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a derby is a match between two sides from the same town, such as Arsenal against Tottenham.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is a famous make of fine English china from the city of Derby, so it names a porcelain.

clue.text: Timidity of NCO towards vices that are fully exposed

indicators.note: to expose something fully is to strip off its covering, so each word loses its outside letters

parts.note: the inside of this word, its ends removed
the inside of this word, its ends removed
the inside of this word, its ends removed

explanation.surface: A sergeant's attitude to his men's bad habits is called spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase about exposure looks like it describes the vices, but it tells you to peel the first and last letter off every word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe lacking courage; cowardice is simply a stronger word for being easily frightened.

clue.text: Working with daughter — it's hearsay

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gossip that the daughter is in work turns out to be rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: The IT comes from the clue word itself, even though 'it's' looks like plain glue before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On-dit is a French borrowing meaning 'they say', used in English for a piece of gossip or rumour.

clue.text: Robin, huge stray who lives next door

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so these letters wander out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes Robin as an enormous wanderer living in the house next to theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin looks like a bird or a name, but it is just letters; 'stray' reads as a noun for a lost dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a descriptive phrase for the person living in the adjoining house, which is what the noun means.

clue.text: Prepare to fence section of two identical planted areas

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut from something longer, so only a run of letters is kept

parts.note: garden written twice; the slice begins with the tail of the first one
the second garden, all but its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a fence around part of a pair of matching flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The string to search is not printed: write garden twice, GARDENGARDEN, and the answer runs across the join. 'Fence' looks like garden work but means swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the call to a fencer to take up the ready position, so it is an instruction to get ready for a bout.

clue.text: Steer university learner part way through obstruction

indicators.note: something put part way through another is pushed into its body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a block is something that obstructs
U is the usual abbreviation for university
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A college student has to drive round a roadblock to get halfway along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like an instruction to drive but it is the noun, a young castrated bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young bull that has been castrated, which is exactly what a bullock is in British usage.

clue.text: Times introduces shortened bible books around annual holiday

indicators.note: introduces means the letter for times comes first, leading the rest in

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: around means the shortened book name is turned to face the other way
shortened means the name loses its last letters

parts.note: Samuel names two books of the Old Testament, 1 and 2 Samuel

explanation.surface: A newspaper running abridged scripture readings around Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bible books' is one name covering two books, 1 and 2 Samuel, so it gives a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is the informal written form of Christmas, a holiday that comes round every year.

clue.text: One extremely leggy girl weed picked up

indicators.note: picking up a signal means catching it by ear, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a girl's name, Millie
weed here is the verb, as in passed water

explanation.surface: Someone notices a girl with very long legs pulling up a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' looks like a garden plant but is the past tense of wee, to urinate; said together, Millie peed sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A millepede (also spelt millipede) is a creature with hundreds of legs, so it is a thing extremely leggy indeed.

clue.text: Hasty sort frames wife

indicators.note: a frame goes all round a picture, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to sift is to sort through
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An impetuous man wrongly pins the blame on his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like a noun for a type of person but is the verb, and 'frames' looks like a false accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and hasty are synonyms, both describing something done quickly or in a hurry.

clue.text: Flight containing two Democrats pursuing European Union

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: flight and wing are both units in an air force

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so this part follows the other

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
D for Democrat, twice

explanation.surface: A plane carrying two American politicians follows the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' reads as one name, but it splits: the first word gives E and the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is the ceremony that joins two people in marriage, so it is a union in that sense.

clue.text: See garland around free, unconfined femme fatale

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: lo is an old word for 'look' or 'see'
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

indicators.note: something unconfined has had its boundaries taken away, so the outer letters go

parts.note: the inside of this word, its ends removed

explanation.surface: Picture a seductress draped in a free flower necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words join as one string and then open up to take the inside of the third word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the siren of German legend whose singing lured Rhine boatmen to their deaths, a classic seductive destroyer.

clue.text: Grass snake, normally bolder, at last retreats

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the letters run backwards, upwards in this down light
at last points to the end, so each word gives its final letter

parts.note: final letter
final letter
final letter

explanation.surface: A grass snake, usually braver, finally backs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass snake' is a real animal, so it is easy to miss that the first word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant, and cereals are members of the grass family, so it is a kind of grass.

clue.text: Gag miserable person that's knocked off first

indicators.note: knocking off the first means removing the opening letter

parts.note: a wretch is an unhappy or pitiable person

explanation.surface: Someone silences a gloomy person before anyone else is dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke or a way to silence someone, but it is the verb for heaving as if to vomit. A wretch loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag and to retch both mean to make the throat movements of vomiting without bringing anything up.

clue.text: President's lot, ever so corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the president's team are all thoroughly dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as possessive but stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt both served as President of the United States.

clue.text: Cave in India, place in fashion

parts.note: India is I in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: one thing put in another sits inside it

parts.note: a mode is a fashion
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A cave in India becomes a trendy place to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a noun for a cavern; with 'in' it is the phrasal verb for collapsing inwards, and India is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to burst or collapse inwards, which is what a roof or wall does when it caves in.

clue.text: Puritan mostly shameful, say, withdrawing benefit

indicators.note: mostly means the word for puritan loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteously moral person, a puritan
vile means shameful or wicked

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the abbreviation for say runs in reverse

parts.note: EG (exempli gratia) means for example, which say also means

explanation.surface: A strait-laced person, rather disgraced, pulls out of a benefits scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PRIG to PRI; 'withdrawing' turns EG into GE at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special advantage or right, a benefit enjoyed by some.

clue.text: Hoaxes involving semi-fake organs

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so the word for hoaxes encloses the half of fake

parts.note: kids means hoaxes or teases, as in you're kidding

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the second half of the word for fake is kept

parts.note: phoney means fake

explanation.surface: Pranks using half-fake body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidneys are a pair of organs that filter waste from the blood.

clue.text: Reckless beloved dropping ecstasy was upset

indicators.note: in a down light, dropping a letter moves it lower, so it shifts to the end and the order changes

parts.note: dear is a term for a loved one

indicators.note: upset means tipped over, so in a down light the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: was and lived both mean existed

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who gave up drugs was distressed by their wild behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping reads as giving up, but here the E of DEAR falls further down the column. 'Was' looks like grammar but means 'lived'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dare-devil works as an adjective for someone who takes bold, foolhardy risks without thought of the danger.

clue.text: Female doctors checking Emergency Room guides

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or stop, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: holders of a doctorate
ER is the abbreviation for emergency room

explanation.surface: Women doctors inspecting a hospital casualty unit show people around.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctors are not medics but holders of doctorates, PhDs.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd is to herd or steer people along, so both words are verbs for leading others where they should go.

clue.text: State's anger about riches being halved

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for anger is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: being halved means only the first half of the word for riches is kept

parts.note: treasure is riches

explanation.surface: A country's fury over its wealth being cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IRE to ERI; 'being halved' cuts TREASURE to TREA. The 's is short for is, linking the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, an independent state since 1993.

clue.text: "Little air" — brief sign north of completely dry area

indicators.note: north of means above in this down clue, so the shortened sign comes first
brief means cut short, so the star sign loses its last letter

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
TT is short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol at all

explanation.surface: A short astrological sign placed above a parched region, captioned as a little tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Air here is a tune, as in an aria, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short aria, a little song in an opera or cantata.

clue.text: Playfully resume chasing black cat?

indicators.note: to chase is to run after, so this part comes second

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: doing something playfully means messing about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitten starts up its game again, pouncing on a dark-furred moggy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the black on the cat, but black is just B and the cat alone is the definition, with a question mark because it is one breed among many.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burmese is a breed of domestic short-haired feline originating in Southeast Asia, so it is an example.

clue.text: Viewed cryptically, I entered plot with prejudice

indicators.note: read the crossword way, a word for going in also tells you to put one thing inside another

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed
taken as written
entered read as 'got into'

explanation.surface: Someone joined a conspiracy, admitting a biased outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a conspiracy but is a flower bed, and 'entered' read as 'got into' supplies both the GOT and the instruction to put it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bigoted is intolerant and unfairly biased, so the phrase means the same thing as an adjective.

clue.text: Raining lightly leaving sierra, very hot on drive

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the shortened hot word follows the abbreviation for drive

parts.note: DR is the address abbreviation for drive, as in a street name

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for sierra departs from the word for very hot

parts.note: sizzling means very hot
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Light rain, a trip away from the mountains, and a scorching road.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To drizzle is to rain in fine light drops, so drizzling means raining lightly.

clue.text: Fool departs with number one bishop

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
number one is a nursery euphemism for urinating, a wee
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: An idiot leaves alongside the most senior bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a top-ranking person but is the childish term for a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a dull, foolish or socially awkward person, a twit or nerd.

clue.text: Extremely obese, following unknown health app

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so this part goes second

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A very overweight person takes up a little-known fitness app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like 'very' but asks for the ends of the next word. Mathematicians use x, y and z for unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: ZOE is a nutrition and gut-health company whose smartphone program tracks diet, so it is the name of a wellness application.

clue.text: Complexity of murder using heart transplant?

indicators.note: a transplant swaps an old organ for a new one, so the central letter is replaced

parts.note: murder causes a death; its central letter A is taken out

explanation.surface: A thriller plot hinges on killing someone by way of an organ swap.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle A of DEATH is swapped for P. The clue does not say where the new letter comes from, which the question mark owns up to; the crossings and the definition settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth can mean intricacy or profundity, as in a novel of real depth, so it matches complexity as a noun.

clue.text: Monkey quietly very active, chucking article

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

indicators.note: chucking means throwing out, so the article is thrown out of the phrase for very active

parts.note: on the go means busy and very active
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A monkey quietly busy, tossing things around.
explanation.definitionFit: Pongo is an old name for a great ape, and the genus name for the orang-utans.

clue.text: He is one small part of something bigger

definitions.note: a sentence, not a noun: He is one of these
definitions.meaning: first meaning: He is the chemical symbol for helium
second meaning: a component or constituent

explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man, but it is the chemical symbol for helium, the second entry in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is a chemical substance in the periodic table, and the same word also means a component or ingredient of a larger whole.

clue.text: Religious composer's first run away from publican

indicators.note: first says it is the earlier of the two Rs in the word for publican that goes
away from means the letter for run is taken out of the word for publican

parts.note: a taverner is an old word for an innkeeper, someone who keeps a tavern
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sacred composer's first escape from an innkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: TAVERNER has two Rs; 'first' picks the earlier one, so 'away from' leaves TAVENER. The 's stands for is, linking the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Tavener was an English composer known for his religious choral music, such as The Protecting Veil.

clue.text: Arm of Warner Brothers somewhat taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
somewhat means to some degree, so only part of the phrase is used

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A division of the Hollywood studio is a little startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a branch of a company, which suits the studio, but it is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bren was a British light machine gun of the Second World War, and arms are weapons.

clue.text: Annelids "do" ground plants

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, as coffee is, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Earthworms make their home in the soil among the vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil and 'plants' like a verb, but one is the anagram signal and the other the definition. Annelids are segmented worms.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandelions are common yellow-flowered weeds, so they are examples of flowering vegetation.
